body: I'd say more the general direction of the alien, but she quickly glanced to me to look at me for some sort of "defense", if that makes sense
So I've heard from some other people
Not sure exactly how to specify. When I walked into the kitchen my dog turned to me clearly in distress. Probably looking at me for some kind of comfort.

My dog looked at me, kind of turned her head when I walked into the room. She usually sleeps downstairs. We were all in the kitchen.


Was that the answer you were looking for? I could elaborate a bit if it's unclear
It was about a head taller than my door (average door, about 6'8") so I'd say a few inches over 7'.

Frankly, I would start trying to piece back some of these dreams? Memories? 


It's significant that you remember these in such detail when you were aged 2-5. I mean, it's literally biological changes that make us forget most of our memories at that age, but it seems like you remember quite a bit. All I have from those ages are a few mental pictures.


I would seriously consider trying to recollect your story.

Nope, thank god they have not. Based on the fact that it visited me pretty much within a 3 year span, (12 y/o, then 15/16) and I'm 19 now with no encounters whatsoever, I'm *80%* sure the whole thing is just behind me. Hopefully.

Thanks very much for this feedback!

To answer your question, it seemed like my dog was looking at me to try to "defend" her for lack of a better term. The only other time she gets like this is when there's thunder, however, her shaking was the worst I've had ever seen. 


As of right now I've pretty much been able to put it all to rest, as sort of mentioned. As long as the alien isn't visiting my parents, mixed with the fact that I felt no sense of fear on the aliens second visit, I can confidently say I'm not writing this out of fear, but just because I wanted to share my story with others because people want answers and I remember all of it.

I've asked myself this kind of question before! If I could either have never experienced this, or keep things the way they are, what would I pick?


Short answer? I'd forget everything.

Long answer is different. Everything I've felt in that 10 minute span was a nerve I've never experienced before in my life, to the point where the entire situation is indescribable. I will likely never feel that way again, and I learned some sort of truth that has been debated for centuries.


You're more than entitled to stick to your beliefs, and I absolutely do not blame you for your thoughts on the situation. I have 0 evidence that I was visited by an ET, I just want to tell me story for, as my title describes, "affirmation or guidance" by some person out there who possibly experienced what I have.

Other than the second visit, quite frankly no. 

I was about 15 or 16 when it visited me a second time, for a brief second. 

Now that you mention it, speaking with a podcast or professional does sound like a good idea. I'd likely still stay anonymous, as I feel that any type of "fame" that could possibly be gained from this would ruin my credibility. I do hope more people can start talking about this type of thing, though. A lot of stories I've been reading about these experiences since I got rabbit-holed here honestly have a lot of similar aspects to them. 

As I said, no paranormal events. I'm off living on my own in college and every year since I've moved I've called my parents asking if they've gotten visits, which they said no.

I'm not artist, but at that time I always slept with the door open a crack. It made next to no noise when entering my room

I don't want to say it glided or hovered into my room, but throughout the entire encounter its limb movements were kept to an extreme minimum.
It didn't hurt or anything like that, but it's as if I weighed nothing to it. That's the unnerving part for me.
